methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series G → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.25x) to $5.7B last post money.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 1 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 2 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
The Boring Company is a Series G stage transportation infrastructure venture with a last post-money valuation of $5.7B and total capital raised of $675M. The transportation sector peer set is limited; while two private comparables exist (Rivian and Einride), neither shares sufficient stage alignment or valuation proximity to support a robust peer-median method.

A stage-progression approach is the applicable triangulation method here. Using a 1.25x step-up multiplier typical of Series G advancement, the $5.7B base valuation implies a forward value of $7.1B. This methodology assumes execution risk aligned with late-stage funding progression and reflects market-standard dilution and value creation patterns at this stage.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $6.1B to $8.2B, with a median point of $7.1B. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow-sector peer comparables at similar stages, limiting the ability to stress-test stage-progression assumptions against market precedent in transportation infrastructure specifically. Capital deployment efficiency and near-term revenue inflection remain material drivers of realized versus implied value. Given the single-method basis, investors should treat this range as directional rather than conclusive.
